title: Triangular polynomial substitution with scalar leading coefficient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $g\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be nonconstant, meaning $g$ is not in the image of the constant-polynomial map $R\to R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. There exist positive integers $e_1,\ldots,e_{n-1}$, an integer $d>0$, a nonzero coefficient $a\in R$ of $g$, and polynomials $b_j\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}]$ for $0\le j<d$, such that $$g(x_1+x_n^{e_1},\ldots,x_{n-1}+x_n^{e_{n-1}},x_n)=a x_n^d+\sum_{j=0}^{d-1} b_j x_n^j.$$ For $n=1$ the exponent list is empty and the displayed substitution is the identity.

source.place: Tag 051N, lemma-helper-polynomial, lines 27963-27994 (with Tag 051M, lemma-helper, in its proof); tags verified in tags/tags.

proof.text:
Use the evaluation homomorphism of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] sending $x_i$ to $x_i+x_n^{e_i}$ for $i<n$ and fixing $x_n$. The image of $x^
u$ is $\prod_{i<n}(x_i+x_n^{e_i})^{
u_i}x_n^{
u_n}$. Expand by distributivity, treating the power with exponent $
u_i$ as a product of $
u_i$ copies. Picking the $x_n^{e_i}$ summand from every copy gives exactly one term $x_n^{w(
u)}$, with coefficient one. Every other choice picks $x_i$ from at least one copy and decreases the exponent of $x_n$ by the sum of the corresponding positive $e_i$. Consequently the image is $x_n^{w(
u)}+h_
u$, where every term of $h_
u$ has $x_n$-exponent strictly less than $w(
u)$. If $w(
u)=0$, there are no other terms. This calculation only uses coefficientwise addition and monomial multiplication, so remains valid over rings with zero divisors or in positive characteristic.

source.place: Tag 051N, lemma-helper-polynomial, proof: leading term of each substituted monomial.

proof.text:
Choose the unique $
u_*\in N$ with maximal weight and set $d=w(
u_*)$ and $a=a_{
u_*}$. A nonzero support vector has a positive coordinate, so the positivity of the weights implies $d>0$. In the finite sum of the monomial expansions from Step 3, the top contribution of $
u_*$ is $a x_n^d$, whereas every other contribution has $x_n$-exponent less than $d$: the other support vectors have strictly smaller weights by Step 2, and each remainder has exponent less than its own weight. Hence the coefficient at $x_n^d$ is exactly $a
e0$, without cancellation. Group all remaining monomials by their $x_n$-exponent $j<d$ to define $b_j\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}]$, using zero for missing exponents. This gives the required formula. For $n=1$ the chosen exponent list and the product over $i<n$ are empty, so the evaluation is the identity and the same argument is the ordinary leading-coefficient calculation.
